A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3STC-HIA work and provide readable text, equations, eight figures and three tables. Both contain 18 pages and end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations on RealisDance-Val and Trajectory100 in Tables 1–2, plus component ablations and qualitative experiments in Table 3 and Figures 5–8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative experiments in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical ground-adaptive motion retargeting and scene-visibility-guided latent fusion procedures, including their inputs, backbone and inference operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RealisDance-Val and Trajectory100 datasets and retain the same terrain, camera-motion and control-combination scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all eight generation-quality comparators. Table 2 retains Tora, RealisDance-DiT and RealisMotion, and Figures 5 and 8 retain the same qualitative comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same 100-clip datasets, first-frame references, trajectory reconstruction and evaluation procedures. The six VBench-I2V dimensions, FID/FVD and translation/yaw error metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3, Table 3 and Figures 6–8 retain identical analyses of ground adaptation, scene-guided camera control and combinations of control signals.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results in Figures 5–8 are identical. For example, Table 2 reports the same 3STC-HIA translation error of 0.478 m and rotation error of 0.162 degrees.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, geometric definitions and equations (1)–(10) are identical, including the trajectory updates, visibility mask and latent fusion. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain identical claims about joint motion and camera control, adaptation to scene geometry, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of component effects, control combinability and FID/FVD tradeoffs are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same future directions concerning richer human-scene interactions and multi-person motion control.

D1.justification: The preprocessing, pretrained models, numerical hyperparameters and project-page access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgement provides no new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the research positioning are identical. All 52 references retain the same content; apparent differences on pages 15–18 result solely from pagination.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgement of UKRI-AHRC CoSTAR National Lab support, grant AH/Y001060/1, on page 15 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgement shifts the reference-list layout and page breaks across pages 15–18. All figures and tables remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–14 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: v3 adds funding credit and updates the version stamp, with minor reference-list reflow. The methods, evidence, claims, explanations and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the revision makes no meaningful difference to overall paper quality.
